question: to the Commission Yannis Maniatis (S&D) Subject:

Turkish provocation in the Eastern Mediterranean region is growing by the day. A case in point is the Great Sea Interconnector between Greece and Cyprus. Türkiye is using military means to obstruct the laying of fibre-optic cables between Astypalaia and Amorgos. Specifically, the Turkish Navy hailed the cable-laying vessel, asking it to stop its work and leave the area. This project is part of the wider fibre optic interconnection project SEA-SPINE (High-speed Submarine Backbone for islands of the Aegean Sea) and is among the EU's priorities, receiving funding from the Connecting Europe Facility (CEF). Given that the Türkiye 2025 report states that ‘violations of Greek territorial waters continued to be reported, with a noticeable increase in incidents compared with the previous reporting period’ and that the maritime zones of EU Member States are becoming increasingly important for its green and digital transition, can the Commission say: 1.
What measures is it considering to defend the EU’s interests in the maritime zones of its Member States against illegal actions by non-EU countries?

Has the Greek Government officially informed the Commission about the above developments and, if so, have joint initiatives been taken to protect this strategic European infrastructure which is co-funded by the CEF?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.5.2026) The EU remains committed to defending its interests and those of its Member States as well as to upholding regional stability. In this context, the EU attaches the greatest importance to safeguarding the sovereign rights of all Member States, in full respect of international law. Unequivocal commitment to international agreements and the UN Charter, as well as abstaining from unilateral actions which violate international law and the sovereign rights of Member States, remains an essential requirement to ensure a stable and secure environment in the Eastern Mediterranean and the development of a cooperative and mutually beneficial relationship between the EU and Türkiye. The Commission is aware of reports regarding the alleged obstruction of cable-laying activities under the SEA-SPINE project co-funded by Connecting European Facility (CEF Digital)1, which aims to enhance digital connectivity between Greek islands and it is a strategic priority for the EU’s digital transition. Following inquiries via European Health and Digital Executive Agency, the consortium confirmed that the Ocean Link vessel completed its scheduled works between Amorgos and Astypalaia without disruption. While no formal notification of hailing was received, the Commission underscores that all EU-funded infrastructure projects operate in full compliance with international law (UN Convention on the Law of the Sea2). The EU rejects any unilateral actions that impede lawful activities. Given the critical role of submarine cables in securing the EU’s digital resilience, the Commission is in close cooperation with Member States to ensure the smooth completion of the project and will continue to monitor closely the situation and the project’s implementation.
